questions.question: In which year was the first Senior Women's National Football Championship held in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first Senior Women's National Football Championship was held in India in **1992**.
 
• This championship was introduced to promote women's football in the country.
 
• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) organized the tournament.
 
• The inaugural tournament witnessed participation from various states across India.
 
• It has since become an annual event, fostering the growth of women's football nationwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All India Football Federation (AIFF)**

 
 
• AIFF is the governing body for football in India.
 
• It was founded in 1937 and is affiliated with FIFA, the global governing body for football.
 
• AIFF is responsible for organizing national competitions and promoting football at all levels.
 
• It oversees both men's and women's football activities in India.
 
 
 
• **Growth of Women's Football in India**
 
 
• Women's football in India has gained significant momentum over the past few decades.
 
• Various national and regional tournaments are held to encourage participation.
 
• The Indian Women's National Football Team has competed in several international tournaments.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to improve infrastructure and training facilities for women footballers.
 
 
 
• **Importance of National Championships**
 
 
• National championships provide a platform for players to showcase their talent.
 
• They help in identifying and nurturing future stars of the sport.
 
• Such tournaments promote a competitive spirit and improve the overall standard of the game.
 
• They also help in building a strong foundation for the national teams.
 
 
 
• **Women's Football Initiatives by AIFF**
 
 
• AIFF has launched several initiatives to boost women's football.
 
• These include grassroots programs, coaching camps, and talent scouting missions.
 
• AIFF also collaborates with international bodies for technical support and training.
 
• There is a focus on increasing participation at the school and college levels.

questions.question: Which edition of the ODI Cricket World Cup was held in India in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2023 ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup was the **13th edition** of the tournament.
 
• It was hosted solely by **India** for the first time, although India had co-hosted earlier editions in 1987, 1996, and 2011.
 
• The tournament featured a total of **10 teams**, competing in a round-robin format followed by knockouts.
 
• The event was organized by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)**, which is the global governing body for cricket.
 
• India became the first country to host the ODI Cricket World Cup independently, highlighting its growing stature in international cricket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ODI Cricket World Cup**

 
 
• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup is the premier international championship of One Day International (ODI) cricket.
 
• The tournament has been held every four years since its inception in 1975.
 
• Australia is the most successful team, having won the tournament five times.
 
 
 
• **2023 World Cup Format**
 
 
• The tournament followed a round-robin format where all 10 teams played against each other once.
 
• The top four teams advanced to the semi-finals, leading to the final match to determine the champion.
 
 
 
• **Past ODI World Cups in India**
 
 
• India co-hosted the 1987 World Cup with Pakistan, the first time the tournament was held outside England.
 
• India co-hosted again in 1996 with Pakistan and Sri Lanka, and in 2011 with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.
 
• India won the 2011 edition, defeating Sri Lanka in the final at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Key Players and Teams**
 
 
• Top cricketing nations like India, Australia, England, Pakistan, and New Zealand participated in the 2023 World Cup.
 
• Key players included Virat Kohli (India), Joe Root (England), Babar Azam (Pakistan), and Trent Boult (New Zealand).

questions.question: Which track and field event has a water jump?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steeplechase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Steeplechase** is an athletics event that involves running and hurdling over obstacles, including a water jump.
 
• The water jump is a pit filled with water, positioned immediately after a hurdle, requiring athletes to leap over both the hurdle and the water.
 
• It is predominantly run over a distance of **3000 meters** in international competitions.
 
• The event is derived from horse racing and was first introduced in the athletics program at the **1900 Paris Olympics**.
 
• It is a test of endurance, speed, and agility, with athletes needing to clear a total of **28 hurdles** and **7 water jumps** during the race.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Steeplechase:**

 
 
• The event originated in Ireland, where horse races involved jumping over streams and stone walls between steeples of churches.
 
• The transition to human athletics began in the mid-19th century in England.
 
 
 
• **Water Jump Design:**
 
 
• The water pit is approximately **3.66 meters (12 feet) long** and slopes upward from a depth of **70 centimeters (28 inches)** at the base.
 
• Athletes must use momentum and technique to minimize contact with water and maintain speed.
 
 
 
• **Famous Athletes:**
 
 
• Kenyan runners have traditionally dominated the steeplechase, with legends like **Ezekiel Kemboi** and **Conseslus Kipruto** winning multiple Olympic and World Championship titles.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Events:**
 
 
• Unlike hurdles or decathlon, steeplechase uniquely includes water obstacles, adding complexity to the race.
 
• Cross-country running lacks artificial obstacles and is conducted over natural terrains.

questions.question: The first ICC Women's T20 Cricket World Cup was hosted by _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**England**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first ICC Women's T20 Cricket World Cup was held in **England** in 2009.
 
• This tournament marked the inception of the Women's T20 World Cup, organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• England emerged as the champions of the inaugural tournament by defeating New Zealand in the final.
 
• The final match of the tournament was played at the iconic Lord's Cricket Ground in London.
 
• The tournament featured a total of 8 teams participating from around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Women's T20 World Cup**

 
 
• It is a biennial international championship for women's Twenty20 International cricket.
 
• The tournament is organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• It aims to promote women's cricket and increase its popularity globally.
 
• Australia has been the most successful team in the tournament's history with multiple titles.
 
• The tournament provides a platform for showcasing talent and increasing the visibility of women's cricket.
 
 
 
• **Lord's Cricket Ground**
 
 
• Known as the "Home of Cricket," Lord's is one of the most famous cricket grounds in the world.
 
• It is located in St John's Wood, London, and is owned by Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).
 
• Lord's has hosted numerous historic matches, including World Cup finals and Test matches.
 
• The ground is named after its founder, Thomas Lord.
 
• It features the famous Long Room and the iconic Media Centre.
 
 
 
• **International Cricket Council (ICC)**
 
 
• The ICC is the global governing body for cricket.
 
• It was founded as the Imperial Cricket Conference in 1909 and later renamed the International Cricket Council in 1989.
 
• The ICC is responsible for organizing major international cricket tournaments, including the Cricket World Cup and T20 World Cup.
 
• It sets the rules and regulations for the sport and promotes the growth of cricket worldwide.
 
• The ICC has over 100 member countries, including full members, associate members, and affiliate members.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first event in a triathlon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swimming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Swimming** is the first discipline in a triathlon event.
 
• A standard triathlon consists of three sequential endurance disciplines: swimming, cycling, and running.
 
• The swimming portion typically takes place in open water, such as a lake, river, or ocean, though some events use pools.
 
• The distance of the swim leg can vary depending on the specific type of triathlon (e.g., Sprint, Olympic, Ironman).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Triathlon Types**

 
 
• **Sprint Triathlon:** Typically involves a 750m swim, 20km bike ride, and 5km run.
 
• **Olympic Triathlon:** Features a 1.5km swim, 40km bike ride, and 10km run.
 
• **Ironman Triathlon:** Comprises a 3.8km swim, 180km bike ride, and 42.2km marathon run.
 
 
 
• **Transition Areas**
 
 
• Triathlons include transition areas where athletes switch from swimming to cycling (T1) and from cycling to running (T2).
 
• These transitions are considered the "fourth discipline" of triathlon due to their strategic importance and timing.
 
 
 
• **Triathlon Gear**
 
 
• Athletes typically use wetsuits in colder water for the swimming leg to enhance buoyancy and reduce drag.
 
• Specialized triathlon bikes are used for the cycling portion, designed for speed and efficiency.
 
• Running shoes and sometimes elastic laces are used to facilitate a quicker transition.
 
 
 
• **Training and Preparation**
 
 
• Triathletes follow structured training plans to balance endurance and skill development across all three disciplines.
 
• Nutrition and hydration are critical components of a triathlete's training and race-day strategy.

questions.question: Australia won the Men's T20 World Cup Cricket in 2021 defeating New Zealand by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8 wickets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Australia defeated New Zealand by **8 wickets** to win the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021.
 
• The final match was held on **14 November 2021** at the Dubai International Stadium, UAE.
 
• New Zealand scored **172/4 in 20 overs**, with Kane Williamson contributing an impressive 85 runs.
 
• Australia chased the target successfully, scoring **173/2 in 18.5 overs** with Mitchell Marsh (77*) and David Warner (53) leading the charge.
 
• This victory marked **Australia's maiden ICC Men's T20 World Cup title**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC T20 World Cup:**

 
 
• The ICC T20 World Cup is an international cricket championship of Twenty20 cricket organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• It was first held in **2007** in South Africa, where India emerged as the inaugural champion.
 
 
 
• **Mitchell Marsh's Performance:**
 
 
• Mitchell Marsh was awarded **Player of the Match** in the final for his unbeaten 77 runs off 50 balls.
 
• His innings included 6 fours and 4 sixes, making it pivotal in Australia's victory.
 
 
 
• **David Warner's Contribution:**
 
 
• David Warner scored 53 runs off 38 balls in the final, setting the pace for Australia's chase.
 
• He was named the **Player of the Tournament** for scoring 289 runs in the competition.
 
 
 
• **New Zealand's Performance:**
 
 
• Kane Williamson's knock of 85 off 48 balls was the highlight of New Zealand's innings.
 
• Despite his efforts, New Zealand was unable to defend their total of 172/4.
 
 
 
• **Venue and Conditions:**
 
 
• The final was played under lights at the **Dubai International Stadium**, known for its batting-friendly conditions.
 
• The dew factor played a role, making it easier for Australia to chase under favorable conditions.

• The Paralympic Games are an **international multi-sport event** for athletes with disabilities, held parallel to the Olympic Games.

questions.question: What was the name of the official torch for the Khelo India University Games 2022?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Shakti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The official torch for the **Khelo India University Games 2022** was named **Shakti**.
 
• The name **Shakti**, which translates to **power** or **strength** in Sanskrit, symbolizes the spirit of energy, determination, and resilience embodied by athletes.
 
• The torch was designed to represent the **core values of the Games**, such as inclusivity, unity, and sportsmanship.
 
• The **Khelo India University Games** is a flagship initiative by the Indian government aimed at promoting sports at the grassroots level and encouraging youth participation in athletics.
 
• The torch serves as a **symbolic representation** of the passion and commitment of participating athletes and fosters a sense of pride and camaraderie among them.
 
• The unveiling of the torch marked the **beginning of the Games**, which focus on nurturing talent and fostering a culture of sports in India.
 
• The naming of the torch as **Shakti** aligns with the themes of **women empowerment** and the importance of strength in achieving excellence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ujala**__

 __
 
• **Ujala** generally symbolizes **light and brightness**, but it was not chosen as the name of the torch for the Khelo India University Games 2022.
 
• The term is often associated with initiatives such as the **Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All (UJALA) scheme**, which promotes energy efficiency in India.
 
 
 
• **Mitra**__
 __
 
• **Mitra** means **friend** or **companion** in Sanskrit, emphasizing harmony and collaboration.
 
• While the term aligns with values of teamwork, it was not selected as the name for the torch.
 
 
 
• **Samarth**__
 
 
• **Samarth** translates to **capable** or **competent**, reflecting qualities of self-reliance and efficiency.
 
• Although the term embodies attributes desirable in athletes, it was not designated as the name of the torch.
